title: Standard evaluation criteria and routing taxonomy for customer data-controls requests
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Purpose: Create a repeatable, auditable evaluation rubric and routing taxonomy for non-bug customer requests about data governance controls (logging redaction, retention, PII handling, audit exports). Goal is to reduce ad-hoc handling, accelerate SLAs for enterprise customers, and surface high-risk requests for Security/Legal review. This ticket scopes the PM-owned criteria, the routing destinations, and an initial lightweight scoring spreadsheet to drive assignment and SLAs.
background: We receive frequent customer asks that look similar but have different risk profiles: short retention window changes, requests to redact logs for PII, export formats for compliance, and one-off audit exports. Current handling varies by channel (support, solutions eng, direct SRE emails) and lacks a consistent prioritization signal. This causes inconsistent SLA delivery, duplicated engineering effort, and missed compliance escalations.
proposed_flow: 1) Intake: Customer submits request via enterprise controls intake form (or via SE triage). Metadata captured: request_type, dataset, retention_change, PII_flag, regulatory_impact, requester_org
2) Auto-score: Lightweight scoring engine (spreadsheet first) computes sensitivity and effort estimate buckets
3) Route: Based on score, route to one of: Console self-serve config, Solutions Eng + PM, Security/Compliance review, or Engineering RFC for infra work
4) SLAs & owner: Assign SLA per bucket (48h, 7d, 30d) and owner team; record in triage spreadsheet and update customer within SLA
5) Implement & Verify: Owner delivers change, QA verifies PII redaction or retention behavior, and logs audit events in the ticket
6) Close with postmortem for any high-impact or delayed items
evaluation_criteria: Data sensitivity: Does the request involve PII, PHI, or other regulated data? (Yes/No)
Regulatory driver: Is there a legal/regulatory requirement (GDPR, HIPAA, FINRA) vs. customer preference?
Scope: One-off export vs. platform-level policy change
Impact surface: Number of customers/orgs affected and downtime or data loss risk
Operational complexity: Engineering changes required (config, infra, storage), estimated effort bucket (S, M, L)
Reversibility: Can the change be rolled back or does it require migration of existing logs/data?
Auditability: Does the request require additional audit logs or evidence for compliance?
Security dependency: Does Security/Legal need to review before implementation?
Time sensitivity: SLA/regulatory deadline or not
Cost implication: Expected recurring storage/compute cost delta
prioritization_rubric: Score components: sensitivity(0-3) + regulatory(0-3) + scope(0-2) + complexity(0-2) + time_sensitivity(0-2)
Total score range: 0-12; buckets: 0-3 Low, 4-6 Medium, 7-9 High, 10-12 Critical

Bucket actions: Low -> self-serve/documentation or next quarter backlog; Medium -> PM+SE review within 7 days; High -> PM+Eng plan within 5 days; Critical -> Security + Exec notice, target 48h response
Tie-breakers: prioritize regulatory-driven and customer SLA-impacting requests over cosmetic or single-user asks
routing_taxonomy: Self-Serve Console Setting: Simple retention/visibility toggles that can be exposed in Console with docs and no infra change
Solutions Eng + PM Runbook: Customer-specific configurations or exports that require SE involvement and scripted workarounds
Security/Legal Review: Any request flagged PII/PHI or with legal/regulatory implications
Engineering RFC & Implementation: Platform changes (schema, retention policy engine, audit export format) that require code and rollout
Dedicated/Enterprise Ops: For customers on Dedicated/Private where changes require per-tenant migration or policy enforcement
acceptance_criteria: A documented rubric (human-readable) exists in Confluence and is linked from the enterprise intake form
Routing taxonomy implemented as options in the intake form and triage spreadsheet maps to owner teams
Triage spreadsheet prototype accepts sample requests and produces consistent assignments for 20 historical requests
SLA targets defined for each score bucket and communicated to Solutions Eng and Support
One pilot with SE+PM on a real customer request executed using the rubric and documented outcome

updates: 2026-03-03: Draft rubric circulated to Security and Legal. Security requested explicit PII flag and examples of PHI. Legal asked to add regulatory drivers as a top-level criterion.
2026-03-05: Engineering flagged ENG-2110 dependency — retention policy engine work may shift some Medium items into High due to migration cost. We added complexity weighting to rubric.
2026-03-08: Design crit with Asha; intake UX updated to capture 'regulatory_deadline' and 'data_schema_samples' to reduce back-and-forth. Accepted with minor changes.

2026-03-10: Pilot run on 20 anonymized requests from last 6 months. Results: rubric produced consistent bucket for 85% of cases. Discrepancy analysis attached in Confluence. Action: adjust scores for single-tenant exports.

2026-03-12: PM + SE executed live pilot with AcmeCorp export request. Routing taxonomy sent to SE, implementation delivered as Solutions Eng runbook, SLA met. Customer confirmed audit export format meets compliance needs. Next: automate scoring in intake form.
decisions: Adopt numeric scoring with explicit weights rather than free-text triage to improve repeatability
Require Security/Legal review for any request with 'PII_flag' or regulatory driver score >=2
Use a two-week pilot window for adjustments before rolling out to broader teams
Start with a spreadsheet-based scoring engine and migrate to an API-driven triage service if pilot shows ROI
